body:
WHAT
A local brain editor, started with `npm run brain-editor` (tools/brain-editor/, TypeScript run by tsx, node:http, no new dependencies — the gateway's pattern, docs/decisions/0002). One page shows the whole brain: the system prompt sections in order, conditional sections, reminders, end-of-turn rungs, background calls, tool descriptions and parameter texts, which tools each context offers (availability.json), and every behaviour knob with its range and meaning (behavior.json, from BEHAVIOR_SPEC). Each item can be edited and saved. The page uses MAGENTRA's teal theme with an animated brain map that doubles as the section navigation.

The same core module answers a command line made for agents: `check`, `show`, `plan <changes.json>`, `apply <changes.json>`, `new-profile <dir>`, all with JSON output. A change is a small typed JSON object (prompt.update, prompt.create, prompt.delete, tool.update, availability.update, behavior.set, behavior.override, file.write). The page sends the same objects to the same functions.

WHY
The owner wants to change MAGENTRA's brain from one place, and wants agents to build new brain profiles later through a path that cannot leave a broken brain behind. brain/ has strict byte-level file rules; hand edits break them easily.

HOW IT STAYS SAFE
- tools/brain/compile.mjs stays the only judge. Every save is applied to a staged copy and compiled with { complete: true }; the save is written only when there are no new problems and every edited prompt or tool text compiles back to exactly the text asked for.
- A change names the brain revision it was planned against; if the folder changed since (another agent, a git checkout), the save is refused.
- Writes are atomic per file. A failed save writes nothing.
- In the shipped brain/, a change to pinned or baseline-held text (core system sections, tool texts, behavior.json, availability.json, other prompts) lists the test it moves and is refused until the caller acknowledges it. The editor never runs npm run approve.
- The server binds 127.0.0.1 only and refuses writes without its action header, as the gateway does.
- `--brain <dir>` edits another brain folder; `new-profile <dir>` copies a brain into a new, empty folder. The engine still builds from brain/ only; choosing a profile at run time is a later phase.
- A Build button runs `npm run build`, and the page shows whether the engine's generated module is current.

WHERE
tools/brain-editor/src/{compiler,format,model,project,server,cli}.ts and src/ui/. Root package.json gains `brain-editor` and `typecheck:brain-editor`. compile.mjs is not changed.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. The editor's view of the shipped brain equals what compileBrain returns: every prompt, tool, parameter, tool set and knob.
2. A saved prompt, tool and parameter text round-trips byte for byte, leading and trailing whitespace included.
3. A change that breaks the brain (bad slot, out-of-range knob, unknown tool) writes nothing and returns the compiler's own problem text.
4. A change planned against an older revision is refused and writes nothing.
5. In the shipped brain a pinned change is refused without acknowledgement and names the pin; in a profile folder it is not.
6. new-profile makes a complete brain the compiler accepts and never overwrites an existing folder.
7. The server answers only on 127.0.0.1, serves the page, and refuses a write without the action header.
8. The command line plans and applies the same change the page does, with JSON output and a non-zero exit on refusal.
